documents.content: The selected vector database must be self-hostable.
Budget for vector database selection is $100k per year.
Only trust primary benchmark data measured internally; ignore vendor marketing numbers for evaluation.

pgvector provides vector similarity search as a PostgreSQL extension. It supports HNSW indexing with high recall (~95%) and low latency (~40ms p95) for large datasets (10M vectors). Key advantages include leveraging existing Postgres infrastructure/backups, seamless metadata filtering via SQL, and no new operational overhead. Limitations include single-node vertical scaling (unless using Citus) and lack of built-in quantization in the tested version.

Qdrant is a vector database written in Rust. Key features include high performance (p95 ~12ms at 10M vectors with 97% recall), significant memory optimization via binary quantization (up to 32x reduction), and strong payload filtering capabilities. It can be self-hosted or used as a managed service.

Weaviate is an open-source vector database with a GraphQL-flavored API. It supports hybrid search (BM25 + vector), which improves relevance on short queries. Performance metrics show p95 ~15ms at 10M vectors with 96% recall. It has a modular architecture for rerankers and vectorizers but has a higher operational footprint compared to other candidates.
The annual budget for the vector database selection is $50k per year.
